instantiated_cells.justification: Legislative agents file expenditure statements with updated registration statements due Jan/May/Sep (every four months), not annually.
The statute requires filings three times per year (Jan/May/Sep) covering four-month periods, not monthly.
Legislative agents must file spending statements with updated registrations on the last day of January, May, and September (a tri-annual schedule), which is an 'other' cadence.
Required filings are every four months (three times per year), not quarterly.
Legislative agents must file expenditure statements tri-annually with updated registrations, so the required cadence is not semi-annual.
Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) are due by the last day of January, May, and September each year, i.e., three times annually (tri-annual).

cell.value: Tri-annually: updated registration statement and expenditure statement due by the last day of January, May, and September each year (covering four-month periods).

instantiated_cells.justification: The statute specifies updated registration filings by the last day of January, May, and September, and expenditure statements are filed with those updates covering the preceding four-month period.

Legislative agents must itemize reportable expenditures by recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client, with a special itemization threshold for meals over $50.
A legislative agent files a statement of expenditures with each updated registration statement due the last day of January, May, and September (three times per year).
Updated registration statements must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the legislative agent actively advocated during the covered period.
The legislative agent expenditure and registration statement provisions do not require disclosure of the amount of compensation received from an employer/client.
The required filings address registrations, expenditures, and financial transactions, but do not require reporting of specific lobbying contacts/communications.
When itemization is triggered, the legislative agent must report the specific items of legislation for which each expenditure was made and the client on whose behalf it was made.
Initial registration statements must include a brief description of the type of legislation to which the engagement relates (a general issue/topic description).

The expenditure report provisions require bill/resolution identification in updated registrations rather than only general subjects; the statute does not establish an activity-reporting regime limited to general subjects in the spending report itself.
Reportable 'expenditures' include gifts, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and when made to covered officials they must be reported with required details.

Employers (and by implication the reporting scheme) exclude from 'expenditures' office facility expenses and compensation, and the statute does not create a separate requirement for legislative agents to report indirect, non-compensation lobbying costs as such beyond the defined expenditures to covered officials.

Legislative agents file spending statements with employer and bill/resolution information and must itemize reportable expenditures, but the statute does not require reporting compensation received, yielding only partial fulfillment of the described components.
Registration requires the legislative agent’s name, business address, and occupation, but does not require disclosure of a phone number.
The legislative agent’s updated registration must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the reporting period.
The initial registration statement requires names/addresses and type of legislation, but does not require stating whether the principal’s business is public or private.
The employer/principal’s business address is required, but the statute does not require the employer/principal’s phone number.

Legislative agents file separately per engagement and must list the employer (and real party in interest if different), but the statute does not impose a general requirement to list all principals represented across engagements in a single disclosure.
Updated registrations must list specific bills or resolutions lobbied, and itemized expenditures must identify the specific items of legislation for which the expenditures were made.

The expenditure reporting definitions and statements expressly exclude compensation paid to legislative agents from 'expenditures,' so direct lobbying costs as compensation are not disclosed as part of the spending report.
A legislative agent’s statement of expenditures must show the total amount of expenditures made by the legislative agent during the reporting period.

Legislative agents must file itemized expenditure reports with bill/client information when expenditures meet the statutory criteria, but compensation received is not required, so the regime is partial rather than fully meeting all listed elements.
The statute requires filing expenditure statements with updated registrations but does not expressly require a 'no activity' or zero-expenditure report when no reportable expenditures occurred.

Expenditure reporting is limited to expenditures made to/for covered public officers or employees, and the statute does not require reporting expenditures benefiting household members of those officials.
When reportable expenditures are made, the statement must include recipient name, total amount, description, and approximate date, reflecting itemization rather than only lump-sum reporting.
